title: Functional Sulfur-Doped Biocarbon for Hydrogen Storage: Development of Nanomaterials for Energy Applications
material_description: SKTP | KOH-activated biocarbon from Sargassum spp. (brown macroalgae, washed, sun- and oven-dried, ground through 60 mesh), pyrolysed under N2 and acid washed; the paper's non-doped sample. Also printed as SKPT (Abstract, Section 2.1, Figure 2 caption) and SKPH (Figure 7a panel label, Section 3.6)
purification_method: 2 M HCl (100 mL) with stirring at 95 C and 240 rpm for 1 h to remove KOH impurities; filtered; washed with deionized water (200 mL, 300 rpm), repeated until neutral pH
activation_method: KOH chemical activation: mixed with KOH (90%, Sigma Aldrich) in a 2:1 ratio (as printed), stirred at 95 C and 400 rpm for 4 h, filtered, dried at 60 C for 16 h; pyrolysis in a horizontal tubular oven at 700 C for 2 h, 10 C/min, N2 flow 50 mL/min (Section 2.1; Abstract and Section 3.2 print 900 C)
functional_groups: thiophenic C-S-C, oxidized sulfur (C-SOx-C, S-O at 168.9 eV), C-O, O-C=O (XPS S 2p and C 1s, Table 2, Figure 5a,b)
source_location: main-09, Section 3.6 text ('The hydrogen storage capacity achieved was 0.33 wt% ... for SKTP'); also Abstract (main-01) and Conclusions (main-10); main-10, Figure 7a, highest-pressure point
notes: digitized: 49.695 bar, 0.3285 wt%, archive: HYC-0058_Fig7a_SKTP_filled.json. Temperature printed as 45 C (318.15 K); pressures stated as absolute (Section 2.3). PCI on Quantachrome Isorb-100 (volumetric), adsorption 0.01 to 50 bar in 25 steps, desorption 50 to 0.01 bar in 25 steps. Basis not named; volumetric default excess. Sample mass printed as 'about 0.15 g'. H2 purity printed only as 'chromatographic purity' (no number). Degassing for H2: 200 C, 2 h, dynamic high vacuum (end pressure not stated); BET degassing was 523 K for 5 h under vacuum (Quantachrome Nova 2200). BET range not stated. Pore volume printed as 'Pore Volume' with no qualifier or method, stored as total pore volume; average pore size method not stated. Branch: the merged plotted point is the highest-pressure marker of Figure 7, drawn as a filled circle (caption: filled = desorption); no open (adsorption) marker is drawn at 50 bar, so it is the turnaround point between the hydriding run (0.01 to 50 bar) and the dehydriding run; the text does not say the value was measured on desorption, coded adsorption. Pressure 50 bar printed in Abstract and Conclusions ('at 45 C and 50 bar', comparison of the two samples); Figure 7 caption 'at 45 C up to 50 bar'. Isotherm point count: 50 markers counted in Figure 7a (25 open, 25 filled). BET 1670 m2/g from Table 1 and Section 3.1; Abstract and Conclusions print 1620 m2/g. Not deliberately doped, but contains native S: 0.85 wt% (CHNS, Table 1), S 2p 0.64 at.% and C 1s 85.61 at.% by XPS (Table 2); C 64.04 wt%, H 3.67 wt%, N not detected; XRD shows sharp peaks the authors attribute to mineral (silica/silicate) impurities; class coded activated_carbon. Raman ID/IG 1.35.
free_volume_calibration: ultrahigh purity He, at 45 C (void volume calibrated after cooling the sample to 45 C)
measuring_lab_id: Barbosa group, Centro de Investigación Científica de Yucatán
